wins.text: Services delivered a record year with revenues of $18.1 billion, up 16% YoY, with RoTCE of 20% for the full year; TTS cross-border transactions up 15% and client wins up 27% with win-loss rate above 80%
USPB revenues increased 14% to $19.2 billion for the full year, with every product up double digits in Q4; branded card interest-earning balances grew 13% and new account acquisition up 8%

Tangible book value per share grew 6% to $86.19 and CET1 ratio increased to 13.3%, approximately 100 bps above regulatory requirement of 12.3%, while returning $6.1 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks

Organizational simplification on track to generate over $1 billion in run-rate saves from net elimination of ~5,000 roles by end of Q1 2024; medium-term target of $2B–$2.5B net run-rate saves from 20,000 net headcount reduction
Investment banking revenues increased 27% YoY in Q4, driven by DCM and advisory; banking overall revenues up 22% in the quarter with improved pipeline and CEO confidence

risks.text: Q4 net loss of $1.8 billion and EPS of -$1.16, driven by $1.7B FDIC special assessment, $1.3B reserve build for Argentina/Russia transfer risk, and ~$880M negative revenue impact from Argentine peso devaluation
Full-year revenues ex-divestitures of $77.1 billion missed guidance of $78B–$79B; markets revenues down 6% for the year with significant December slowdown in rates and FX
Wealth RoTCE of only 2.6% for full year on $7.1B revenue; banking RoTCE of -0.2% for full year; both businesses acknowledged as underperforming with significant work remaining
Card NCL rates expected to rise above pre-COVID levels and peak in 2024; branded card NCL rate guided to 3.5%–4.0% and retail services NCL rate to 5.75%–6.25% for full year 2024

Basel III endgame regulatory uncertainty constraining ability to commit to buyback cadence beyond quarter-to-quarter; ongoing transformation and regulatory consent order obligations continue to pressure expenses

guidance_items.detail: 2024 revenue guided to $80B–$81B, above prior full-year 2023 guidance of $78B–$79B (which was missed at $77.1B)
NII ex-markets expected to be down modestly in 2024 as volume growth offset by lower U.S. rates and closed exit/wind-down reduction
Medium-term RoTCE target of 11%–12% by 2026 reaffirmed; modest buybacks expected in Q1 2024
Expenses guided to $53.5B–$53.8B for 2024, down from $54.3B in 2023 (ex-FDIC), with $700M–$1B of elevated severance/simplification costs embedded
Medium-term expense target path to $51B–$53B underpinned by $2B–$2.5B net run-rate saves from 20,000 net headcount reduction (ex-Mexico)

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Historical pattern of failed restructurings at Citi and skepticism about why this time is different
Detailed breakdown of where the remaining ~15,000 headcount reductions (beyond the 5,000 managerial cuts) will come from
Whether revenue guidance embeds any reduction from proposed CFPB credit card late-fee rule changes
